question: In 2025, what does the abbreviation NGLV stand for in ISRO’s latest rocket programme?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Next Generation Launch Vehicle**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **NGLV (Next Generation Launch Vehicle)** is a part of the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)**'s initiative to develop advanced rocket technologies for future space missions.
 
• The **NGLV** is designed to be a successor to ISRO’s existing launch vehicles, such as the **Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle (PSLV)** and **Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle (GSLV)**.
 
• This new launch vehicle aims to meet the demands for launching heavier payloads into various orbits, including **geostationary, low Earth, and deep space missions**.
 
• **NGLV** incorporates cutting-edge technologies such as reusable components, advanced propulsion systems, and improved efficiency to reduce costs and enhance reliability.
 
• It is expected to play a critical role in India’s **future deep space exploration missions** and in meeting the growing demands for satellite launches worldwide.
 
• The development of **NGLV** reflects ISRO’s commitment to advancing India’s space capabilities and ensuring competitiveness in the global space launch market.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO):**

 
 
• **ISRO** is India’s premier space agency, established in **1969** and headquartered in **Bengaluru**. It is responsible for advancing space technology and conducting space missions for civilian and military applications.
 
• ISRO has developed several successful launch vehicles, including the **PSLV**, **GSLV**, and **GSLV Mk III**, which have placed satellites into orbit for communication, navigation, Earth observation, and interplanetary exploration.
 
• **Key achievements:** ISRO's remarkable missions include **Chandrayaan** (India’s lunar exploration program), **Mangalyaan** (Mars Orbiter Mission), and the **Gaganyaan human spaceflight program**.
 
 
 
• **Importance of NGLV:**
 
 
• The **NGLV** is vital for India’s ambition to expand its presence in the space sector, especially in launching heavier payloads and undertaking interplanetary exploration missions.
 
• The vehicle is expected to have **advanced features** such as reusable stages, modular design, and compatibility with various payloads.
 
• It will help India compete globally in the space launch industry, offering cost-effective and reliable solutions for satellite deployments.
 
 
 
• **Existing Launch Vehicles:**
 
 
• **PSLV:** Known for its versatility, PSLV has launched satellites into various orbits, including polar and geostationary transfer orbits. It has been operational since **1993**.
 
• **GSLV:** Designed for heavier payloads and geostationary missions, it incorporates cryogenic engine technology. First launched in **2001**.
 
• **GSLV Mk III:** India’s most powerful rocket, used for heavy payloads and deep space exploration. It was first launched in **2014** and is integral to the **Gaganyaan mission**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Global Space Industry:**

 
 
• The global space industry is valued at around **$400 billion**, with satellite launches being a key contributor.
 
• India has become a key player in offering cost-effective satellite launching services, with ISRO being renowned for its **low-cost missions**.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of NGLV:**
 
 
• **Reusable components:** This feature will reduce costs and make launches more sustainable.
 
• **Advanced propulsion systems:** Allowing for greater efficiency and higher payload capabilities.
 
• **Modular design:** Enabling flexibility to adapt to different mission profiles and payloads.
